## Claims
- [source-backed] The source states that Theorem 5.4 gives two generating sets for \(J_v\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 14-21]
- [source-backed] For \(r\)-Grassmannian data, \(J_v\) is generated in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by the Schur classes \(s_\mu\) with \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [source-2, lines 1365-1375]
- [computed] In the \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,2,3)\) interval, the complete integral Pieri computation gives \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^6\), with nonzero free quotient ranks \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8\), respectively, and no torsion. [artifact 4d073f3d77472c01e4aab7680d125484749048e7697fdb8e3cd287017c08dc5c]
- [proved] Both six-element families
  \[
  \mathcal F_{\rm top}=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},
  \quad
  \mathcal F_{\rm bot}=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}
  \]
  are minimal generating sets of \(J_{2,3}\).
- [proved] The requested \(i=j=p=2,\ c=3\) minimality corollary is established.

## Strategy
Here \(a=\min(p,c)=2\), \(b=\min(i,j)=2\), hence
\[
N=\binom{a+b}{a}=\binom42=6.
\]
Using the accepted interval presentation
\[
J_{2,3}=\bigoplus_{(2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(4^5)}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
\subseteq A=\Lambda/I_{5,4},
\]
and \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)\), task 142 computes
\[
Q:=J_{2,3}/A_+J_{2,3}=J_{2,3}/\Lambda_+J_{2,3}\cong\mathbb Z^6.
\]

By the known six-element generation statements, each displayed family generates \(J_{2,3}\). Thus its images give a surjection
\[
\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6.
\]
After choosing an isomorphism \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\), this is a surjective square integral matrix, hence has determinant \(\pm1\). Therefore the six images form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\).

If a proper subfamily generated \(J_{2,3}\), then its images would generate \(Q\), contradicting that no proper subfamily of a basis of \(\mathbb Z^6\) spans. Hence each family is minimal.

## Gaps
None for this case-specific corollary, conditional only on the accepted interval presentation, task 142 computation, and the known generation statements specified in the task.
